summary: BC Forest Service fire lookout on Old Glory Mountain near Rossland, 1926-1977; rebuilt 1930, replaced 1963 (the museum gives about 1969 for the current structure). The 1968 weather-station fire is a separate building. The Rossland Museum says the lookout was restored in 2016/2017.

facts.design: present building on the summit, replaced in 1963 on more secure foundations (museum gives about 1969)
facts.status_note: Retired from lookout service in 1977. A two-year restoration had begun by 19 August 2016; the Rossland Museum says the Friends of the Rossland Range restored the lookout in 2016/2017. No source I read says whether visitors can reach the summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The board's title gives the range as 1927 to 1977, but its text gives 1926 to 1977 and dates the original building to 1926. The story uses 1926 from the text.
The museum gives 7 January 1968 for the weather station fire and the 100 Mile Free Press gives 2 January. The story gives both and notes that the building was not the lookout.

The board dates the present structure to 1963, when the original building was demolished and replaced. The Rossland Museum page gives 'Current structure ~1969'. The story uses 1963 from the board, which cites Forest Service records, and gives the museum's approximate date as well.

notes_for_editor: Solid history from the 1944 newsletter (via Canada Lookouts), the Friends of the Rossland Range board (2012), and the Rossland Museum page. Gaps: no current access or trail information. The museum page says the Friends of the Rossland Range restored the lookout in 2016/2017 and describes what remains on the summit, but it does not say whether visitors can reach it. The brief's Sites and Trails BC listing (REC2434) returned no text from fetch_text, so the brief's public access and Recreation Sites and Trails BC agency are not confirmed by any text I read. The museum's painting-firm link has no date I could confirm. A Facebook group snippet gives Gibbard's service as 1938 to 1950; not fetched, not used. The weather station is a separate building and is mentioned only to keep it apart from the lookout. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the earlier draft said no source confirmed the restoration was finished; the museum page does say so, and the story now reports it.
